item.title: Trade Deals, Airstrikes, Genocide Rulings, and Arson Convictions: On Air, November 21, 2026
item.description:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham met with European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels on Friday to secure a reset of post Brexit relations through new agreements on food exports, emissions trading, and youth mobility. The agreed sanitary and phytosanitary arrangement removes most post Brexit checks and restrictions on British food and agricultural products starting March 1, 2028, in exchange for the United Kingdom following specified European Union regulations. The two sides also agreed to link their emissions trading systems beginning in January 2028. A youth experience scheme will permit up to 100,000 young citizens from both jurisdictions to live and work abroad for up to three years.
Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by Yemen's Houthi militia toward Riyadh early Saturday, following an earlier Houthi strike that damaged the Public Investment Fund tower and neighboring buildings in the capital. The coalition fighting the Houthis stated that its forces targeted operational capabilities at Hodeidah port used in smuggling operations and weapons transport, alongside military targets in Sanaa, Saada, and Taiz governorates. The Houthi military spokesman asserted that the operation successfully hit vital targets in Riyadh. Independent observers noted potential impacts on the proposed United States and Saudi Arabia nuclear power pact.
NATO aircraft scrambled in response to three objects breaching Polish airspace overnight during a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine that killed at least five people and damaged three bridges in Kyiv. Polish Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz stated that the objects included an Kh-101 cruise missile, another missile, and a jet-powered drone. The Kh-101 missile came down in a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec, about 30 miles from the Ukrainian border and approximately 47 miles from where military exercises were underway. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk characterized the incursion as an intentional Russian provocation, and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte condemned the event.
The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for state-sponsored genocide against its Rohingya Muslim minority during a 2017 military campaign, marking the first time a state has been held responsible for genocide in the court history. Delivered in The Hague by court president Iwasawa Yuji, the ruling was decided by a majority vote of nine to six in a case brought by The Gambia. The court accepted estimates that at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, along with documentation of systematic sexual violence and village burnings. The United Nations court ordered Myanmar to provide safe passage home for refugees, issue reparations, and prosecute individuals involved.
Danish authorities announced on Friday that they thwarted a plot by Russian intelligence services to assassinate Ukrainian-American rapper Kyivstoner, whose real name is Albert Vasiliev, during a concert in a Copenhagen suburb on September 25. Police arrested three men traveling in a car carrying firearms and knives near the venue, with two suspects tied to the gang Loyal to Familia charged with attempted murder and assisting foreign intelligence. In response, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen summoned the Russian ambassador and announced the expulsion of Russia's defense attaché with a seven-day deadline to leave the country. Russian state media asserted that the accusations lacked evidence.
A federal jury in Los Angeles convicted 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht on Friday of two counts of federal arson for starting the Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed over 6,800 structures in January 2025.

item.title: Supreme Court Blocks Grant Cuts, Air Traffic Stalls: On Air, November 17, 2026
item.description:
The United States Supreme Court on Monday rejected an appeal by the Trump administration seeking to cancel tens of millions of dollars in academic research grants awarded to University of California faculty. The justices issued a brief order without noted dissents, leaving intact a preliminary injunction issued by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. The San Francisco-based appeals court held that federal agencies likely violated the First Amendment by terminating funding based on perceived viewpoints. The grants directly before the Supreme Court were awarded to University of California researchers by the National Science Foundation and the National Endowment for the Humanities.
Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping met Tuesday in Shenzhen ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit to agree on additional tariff cuts and deeper economic ties. China will provide tariff relief on approximately 400 million Canadian dollars, equivalent to 280 million US dollars, in Canadian exports, including frozen pork cuts, fish, and seafood. In exchange, Canada will extend tariff exemptions for specific Chinese steel and aluminum products by two years.
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced Monday that he is dissolving the NYPD Strategic Response Group, a specialized counterterrorism and protest response unit formed in 2015. Appearing alongside Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch, Mamdani stated that the unit will be replaced by a civilian-led Community Dialogue and De-escalation Division within the Mayor Office of Community Safety, alongside a specialized NYPD team named the First Amendment Support Team. The new civilian division possesses no weapons or arrest powers, while the directive bans the use of tear gas, pepper spray, long guns, and kettling during First Amendment activities.
United Airlines resolved a widespread system outage on Monday evening that briefly grounded departing flights across the United States. The technology issue began around 3:30 p.m. and lasted for approximately 90 minutes before systems were restored around 6 p.m. Eastern time. The disruption affected pilot-facing applications, including crew communications and messaging systems, and prevented the airline from providing final aircraft weight information required for preflight calculations. Airborne flights and United Express regional services were unaffected by the outage.
U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for the Southern District of Texas issued formal warning letters to congressional Democrats, threatening potential legal consequences over upcoming oversight investigations targeting President Donald Trump and his associates. Reitz accused Senator Elizabeth Warren, Senator Richard Blumenthal, Senator Elissa Slotkin, and Representative Robert Garcia of attempting to weaponize congressional oversight and deprive American citizens of constitutional rights. The Campaign for Accountability filed an ethics complaint against Reitz with the State Bar of Texas over the prosecutor's threats.

The deployment follows months of stalled diplomatic efforts and a collapsed memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran.
